t: The first Persian Empire, built by Cyrus the Great, stretched from the Indus to the Aegean and the Nile.
Darius I's satrapies, Royal Road, coinage and Aramaic chancery became the model for later Near Eastern empires.
Weakened by revolts and court murders, it fell to Alexander the Great in just four years, 334 to 330 BCE.
dyk: Royal couriers on the 2,700-kilometre Royal Road from Susa to Sardis could cover the distance in around a week, using relays of fresh riders.
ev: Cyrus II defeats Astyages and takes over the Median Empire
Cyrus defeats the Babylonians at Opis and enters Babylon
Cambyses II defeats Psamtik III at Pelusium and conquers Egypt
Xerxes invades Greece, wins at Thermopylae, sacks Athens but loses at Salamis
Egypt revolts on the death of Darius II and stays independent for six decades
Alexander the Great defeats Darius III at Gaugamela
Alexander burns Persepolis; Darius III is murdered by his satrap Bessus
